backlog.spec: Exploit the test SMILES, which are available at predict time, through graph smoothing rather than pseudo-labels. Compute 2048-bit radius-2 Morgan presence fingerprints for train and test molecules together as a packed boolean matrix and form the Tanimoto similarity between every molecule and every training molecule using matrix products of the bit matrix (intersection over union). For each molecule keep only its 15 most similar training molecules, zeroing the rest, symmetrise the resulting sparse affinity, and run sklearn.semi_supervised.LabelSpreading(kernel='precomputed'-style handling or an explicit few iterations of F <- alpha * S_norm @ F + (1-alpha) * Y with alpha=0.8 and 30 iterations) over the combined train-plus-test graph with training labels clamped. Rank-transform the resulting test scores and add them as a fourth unit-weight member to the incumbent three-member rank average, then min-max scale.
backlog.title: Transductive label spreading over a Tanimoto neighbour graph

backlog.spec: Compute a parameter-free CNS MPO style score from RDKit values: piecewise-linear desirability for MolLogP (best ≤3), MolWt (best ≤360), TPSA (best 40–90), HBD (best ≤0.5) and the count of basic amines. Sum the desirabilities. Add the rank of this score as a fourth ensemble member with weight 0.5 relative to the weight of 1 for each XGBoost member.
backlog.title: CNS MPO desirability rank member

backlog.spec: Replace the equal weights in the rank average with weights earned on held-out training data. Inside fit_predict, run a 4-fold stratified inner cross-validation on the training set (StratifiedKFold with shuffle=True and random_state=seed) and, for each of the three feature sets, collect out-of-fold predictions from the incumbent XGBoost configuration; compute each feature set's inner AUROC with sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score. Turn the three scores into weights with w = max(auc - 0.5, 0.0), normalised to sum to one. Then refit each member on the full training set as now, rank-transform its test probabilities, combine with those weights, and min-max scale. The inner CV costs 12 extra XGBoost fits per fold, so reduce n_estimators to 300 for the inner fits only and confirm the whole job stays inside 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Weight the rank average by inner out-of-fold AUROC

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 3-fold stratified CV on the training set for each of the three XGBoost members, using 150 rounds for speed. Compute the OOF AUROC of each member. Use weights proportional to max(AUROC-0.5, 0)^2 when rank-averaging the final full-fit members.
backlog.title: Rank-averaging weights from inner OOF AUROC

backlog.spec: Before fitting each XGBoost member, build an augmented training set by stacking the original rows with one copy where each nonzero feature is zeroed with probability 0.15 (seeded numpy RNG). Duplicate the labels. Predict on the unmodified test features.
backlog.title: Input bit-dropout augmentation

backlog.spec: Add a genuinely different function class to the ensemble, since every tree-based fourth member so far has landed in the noise. Keep the three XGBoost members and the rank-averaging structure unchanged, and add a fourth rank-averaged member: an sklearn MLPClassifier fitted on the concatenation of the Morgan presence bits and the MACCS keys, with the atom-pair counts log1p-transformed and appended, all columns standardised with StandardScaler fitted on the training fold only. Use hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), activation='relu', alpha=1e-3, batch_size=64, learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, n_iter_no_change=15, max_iter=300, random_state=seed. To damp the high seed variance of small neural nets, fit three MLPs with random_state seed, seed+1 and seed+2 and average their probabilities before the rank transform; give the averaged MLP the same unit weight as each XGBoost member.
backlog.title: Multilayer perceptron member on folded fingerprints

backlog.spec: Combine the two best-performing single additions into one ensemble. Keep the three existing per-feature-set XGBoost members and their rank contributions. Then build the pooled feature matrix X = hstack(Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS) and add two further rank-averaged members: (a) an ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on X, and (b) a random-subspace XGBoost: 24 XGBClassifier models (n_estimators=200, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.08, subsample=0.8, min_child_weight=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed+k), each fit on a random subset of 30% of the columns of X drawn with a numpy Generator seeded from seed; average the 24 class-1 probability vectors before ranking. Final prediction is the min-max scaled sum of the five rank vectors.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees plus random-subspace XGBoost together

backlog.spec: Augment each member's training set with convex combinations of same-class molecules to smooth the decision surface over scaffold gaps. For each of the three feature sets inside fit_predict, generate extra rows equal to the number of training molecules: sample pairs of training molecules that share the same label (draw from a numpy Generator seeded by seed plus the feature-set index), draw a mixing weight lam from Beta(0.4, 0.4), and set the synthetic row to lam * x_i + (1 - lam) * x_j with the shared label kept exact, so no label mixing is needed. Stack the synthetic rows under the real rows and fit the incumbent XGBClassifier configuration on the combined matrix. Keep the three-member rank average, the min-max scaling and all hyperparameters unchanged, so the only difference is the doubled training matrix.
backlog.title: Feature-level mixup augmentation before boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the final rankdata-based combination with an average of logits. For each member, convert its test probabilities p to log(p/(1-p)) after clipping to [1e-6, 1-1e-6]. Average the logits across members with equal weights, then map the mean back through a sigmoid to get the returned probability of class 1. The output stays in [0,1] and keeps the same ordering semantics, but it preserves the magnitude of confident predictions rather than discarding it.
backlog.title: Logit averaging instead of rank averaging across members

backlog.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member of a completely different model family: a neural network. Pool the three existing feature matrices into X = hstack(Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS), apply log1p to the atom-pair count block (or to all of X, which is harmless for 0/1 blocks), then fit sklearn's MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), activation='relu', alpha=1e-3, batch_size=64, learning_rate_init=1e-3, max_iter=300, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, n_iter_no_change=20, random_state=seed) inside a Pipeline with StandardScaler(with_mean=False). Average the class-1 probabilities over three seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) to tame initialisation noise, rankdata the average, and add it to `total` before the existing min-max scaling.
backlog.title: Multilayer perceptron member on pooled features

backlog.spec: Combine the two best unreplicated single changes into one script, since they lower loss through different mechanisms (model family diversity versus feature decorrelation) and may add. Build the pooled feature matrix by concatenating the three blocks from fingerprints(). First, fit 16 XGBClassifier models with the incumbent hyperparameters (n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2), each on an independent random one-third subset of the pooled columns drawn from a numpy Generator seeded by seed plus member index. Second, fit one ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed) on the full pooled matrix. Rank-transform every model's positive-class test probability with rankdata, give the 16 subspace members total weight 1.0 (so 1/16 each) and the ExtraTrees member weight 0.5, sum, and min-max scale. Keep threads at 8 in total and stay inside the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees member plus random-subspace XGBoost together

backlog.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member that is a similarity-weighted nearest-neighbour classifier, which captures local structure the tree models smooth over. Build RDKit ExplicitBitVect Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test molecules and compute the full test-by-train Tanimoto similarity matrix with DataStructs.BulkTanimotoSimilarity. For each test molecule take its k=15 most similar training molecules and predict sum(s_j^3 * y_j) / sum(s_j^3) over those neighbours (add 1e-9 to the denominator). Rankdata this vector and add it to `total` alongside the three XGBoost rank vectors, then min-max scale as now. The similarity matrix for ~1300 by ~300 molecules is cheap, so runtime barely changes.
backlog.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour member

backlog.spec: Set scale_pos_weight to the ratio of negative to positive training labels, computed inside fit_predict from train_y, in each of the three XGBoost fits. Everything else stays the same, including the seed, the feature sets, and the rank averaging. This reweights the minority class in the gradient and may shift the tree splits toward better separation of the rarer class, which AUROC rewards. It was not tried for the boosting members, only for random forest.
backlog.title: Class-balanced scale_pos_weight in every XGBoost member

backlog.spec: In each of the three XGBoost fits, replace colsample_bytree=0.3 with colsample_bytree=1.0 and colsample_bynode=0.3. Keep every other setting, the seed, and the rank averaging. This changes how feature sampling is applied, from once per tree to once per split, so trees see more varied candidate features within a single tree.
backlog.title: Per-node column subsampling in the XGBoost members

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, add a fourth rank-averaged member: sklearn ExtraTreesClassifier (500 trees, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) trained on the horizontally concatenated Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS matrices. Rank-average it with the three XGBoost members with equal weight, then min-max normalise as before.
backlog.title: Add ExtraTrees member to ensemble (replicate)

backlog.spec: Re-run the slot-27 configuration unchanged to get a second measurement of its 0.0873 result. Replace the three per-feature-set XGBoost fits with a random-subspace ensemble over the pooled feature matrix: concatenate the three feature blocks from fingerprints() (Morgan presence bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS keys) into one matrix, then fit 24 XGBClassifier models, each on an independently drawn random subset of roughly one third of the pooled columns, drawn with a numpy Generator seeded from the seed argument plus the member index. Use the incumbent XGBoost hyperparameters (n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, eval_metric='logloss'), set n_jobs so total threads stay at 8, rank-transform each member's test probabilities with rankdata, sum them, and min-max scale the sum. Watch the 10-minute budget: if 24 members is too slow, drop to 16 but keep everything else identical and say so.
backlog.title: Replicate the random-subspace XGBoost ensemble

backlog.spec: Change each XGBoost member to booster='dart' with rate_drop=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, n_estimators=400, and the other parameters unchanged. Check that runtime stays within the budget. Keep the rank averaging.
backlog.title: DART booster members

backlog.spec: Extend featurize() with about six extra columns that are cheap and BBB-relevant: number of aromatic rings (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumAromaticRings), number of aliphatic rings, heavy-atom count, number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations (MW>500, cLogP>5, HBD>5, HBA>10), halogen count, and amide count from the SMARTS C(=O)N. Keep the existing 10 columns. Feed this 16-column matrix to the existing descriptor-based member only; the three fingerprint XGBoost members stay as they are.
backlog.title: Rule-of-five and ring-count descriptor extension

backlog.spec: Wrap the three-member ensemble so that it is run with 3 different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), using reduced n_estimators=300 per model to stay inside the time limit. Rank-average the member predictions across seeds, then normalise. Reuse the fingerprints computed once.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged ensemble bagging

backlog.spec: Add a rank-averaged member that is a KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=25, weights='distance') on the 10 curated descriptors. Scale them with QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') fitted on the training fold, then apply StandardScaler. Use the predicted probability of class 1 as the member score. The purpose is a local, non-parametric physchem view that differs from both the trees and the linear models.
backlog.title: Quantile-scaled k-nearest-neighbour member on curated descriptors

memo:
Helped: curated 10-feature descriptors (0.1243 vs 0.1361 start). Ensembling three models on different feature sets gave the biggest gain (0.1002). XGBoost in that ensemble gave 0.0934 and 0.0879 (incumbent mean 0.0906).

Did not help: single-model swaps (CatBoost 0.1264, Tanimoto SVC 0.1255, logistic regression 0.1264, LightGBM 0.0979). Also no help: one RF on combined features (0.1011), strong regularization (0.1058), scaffold bagging (0.0995), scaffold weighting (0.0977), self-training (0.0920), count Morgan (0.0912), feature filtering (0.0940), auxiliary regressors (0.0942), naive Bayes (0.0947), GP (0.0926).

Fourth-member additions sit near noise (sd about 0.0049). Best singles: ExtraTrees 0.0866, random-subspace XGBoost 0.0873, Gobbi 0.0880, ErG 0.0884. None replicated.

Next: replicate ExtraTrees and random-subspace first. Then try them together. Accept only if the replicate is below 0.088. Stop small tweaks and new featurizers.
